description: Nucleoid constructs labeled stock snapshots without assigning caller variables
code:
code = "caller"
quantity = 99
class Stock(*, code: str, quantity):
    this.code = code
    this.quantity = quantity
stock = Stock(quantity=4, code="A")
assert(stock.code, "A")
assert(stock.quantity, 4)
assert(code, "caller")
assert(quantity, 99)
stock.quantity

description: Nucleoid inherits an opted-in initializer and leaves omitted parameters null
code:
class Location(*):
    def init(city: str, zone):
        this.city = city
        this.zone = zone
class Depot: Location
    pass
depot = Depot(city="Oslo")
assert(depot.city, "Oslo")
assert(depot.zone, null)
assert(Location.length, 0)
assert(Depot.length, 1)
depot.city

description: Nucleoid forwards ordinary child parameters to a named parent constructor
code:
class Rectangle(*, width, height):
    this.width = width
    this.height = height
class Panel(w, h): Rectangle
    super(height=h, width=w)
panel = Panel(3, 4)
assert(panel.width, 3)
assert(panel.height, 4)
assert(Rectangle.length, 0)
panel.width * panel.height

description: Nucleoid keeps named argument evaluation ordered and constructor values frozen
code:
'use imperative'
class Pair(*, first, second):
    this.first = first
    this.second = second
events = {count: 0}
pair = Pair(second=(events.count=1), first=events.count.value + 1)
assert(pair.first, 2)
assert(pair.second, 1)
events.count = 9
assert(pair.first, 2)
assert(pair.second, 1)
assert(events.count, 9)
pair.first
